q: 341. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete is known as
explain: Bleeding is defined as the upward movement/separation of water (sometimes carrying fine cement and sand particles) from freshly placed concrete, appearing on the top surface.

q: 342. Concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is fundamentally a composite material made up of cement, aggregate, and water together (plus admixtures where used), so all of these are its main constituents.

q: 343. The rock which is not calcareous is
explain: Laterite is an iron/aluminium-rich residual soil/rock formed by weathering, not a calcium-carbonate (calcareous) rock like limestone or chalk.

q: 344. To obtain cement dry powder, limestones and shales or their slurry is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: The raw material slurry/powder of limestone and shale is burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1400°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 345. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO) is present in the highest proportion among the chemical constituents of Portland cement, typically around 60-65%.

q: 346. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
explain: Efflorescence, the white surface deposit seen on concrete and masonry, results from an excess of soluble alkalies in the cement migrating to the surface with moisture.

q: 347. Di calcium silicate
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and generates comparatively less heat of hydration than tricalcium silicate, though it contributes to good long-term/ultimate strength.

q: 348. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage is due to its
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves its high early strength mainly through finer grinding, which increases the surface area available for rapid hydration reaction.

q: 349. For road pavements, the cement generally used is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the general-purpose cement commonly used for road pavement construction as per this text.

q: 350. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction, as it minimizes the heat of hydration and reduces the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 351. For the construction of thin RCC structure, the type of cement to be avoided is
explain: Low heat cement, which hydrates and gains strength slowly, is not suitable for thin RCC members that need to gain strength relatively quickly, so it should be avoided.

q: 352. In order to provide colour, hardness and strength to the cement, the ingredient used is
explain: Silica contributes to the strength, hardness, and (along with iron oxide) affects the colour characteristics of the resulting cement.

q: 353. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved through IS sieve number
explain: The final ground cement is checked for fineness by sieving through IS sieve no. 9 (90-micron sieve) as per standard testing practice.

q: 354. If the fineness modulus of sand is 3, then the sand is graded as
explain: As per the fineness modulus classification used in this text, a value of 3 places the sand in the 'coarse sand' category.

q: 355. The presence of calcium chloride in water
options: causes little effect on quality of concrete
explain: Calcium chloride, when present in mixing water, acts as an accelerator that speeds up both the setting and the hardening of cement, so both a and b occur.

q: 356. If sea water is used for preparing concrete mix, it
explain: Sea water contains salts that reduce concrete strength, promote corrosion of embedded steel reinforcement, and cause efflorescence — all of these harmful effects occur.

q: 357. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag of 50 kg cement are
options: 70 litres of sand and 120 litres of aggregates
70 kg of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix, with one bag of cement corresponding to about 35 litres, the sand requirement (3×35=105 litres) and coarse aggregate requirement (6×35=210 litres) work out to 105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregate.

q: 358. The dimensions of 35 litres forma for measuring aggregates by volume are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 22 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box measuring 22 cm × 25 cm × 40 cm gives a volume corresponding to 35 litres.

q: 359. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using OPC should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the complete process from mixing to compacting concrete made with OPC should be finished within 40 minutes to avoid loss of workability due to initial setting.

q: 360. For reinforced concrete exposed to sulphate attack minimum grade required is
explain: As per the durability requirement referenced in this text, the minimum grade specified for reinforced concrete exposed to sulphate attack is M10.

q: 361. The total chloride content as percentage of mass of cement in concrete mix should be limited
explain: As per durability provisions, the total chloride content in a concrete mix (as percentage of cement mass) should be limited to 0.16% to control the risk of reinforcement corrosion.

q: 362. The maximum water cement ratio in plain concrete to ensure durability in mild exposure is limited to
explain: For plain concrete under mild exposure conditions, the maximum permissible water-cement ratio specified for durability is 0.7.

q: 363. For a given degree of hydration, the effect of increasing water cement ratio in concrete
explain: A higher water-cement ratio results in a more porous cement paste structure with larger and more interconnected capillary pores, thereby increasing the permeability of concrete.

q: 364. For a given water cement ratio, with passage of time, the permeability
explain: As hydration continues over time, the cement gel progressively fills the capillary pore structure, which decreases the permeability of concrete for a given water-cement ratio.

q: 365. As compared to moist cured concrete, the permeability of steam cured concrete is
explain: Steam curing, due to its accelerated hydration process, tends to produce a coarser pore structure, resulting in higher permeability compared to normally moist-cured concrete.

q: 366. Colocrete is the commercial term for
explain: 'Colocrete' is a commercial/trade term referring to coloured cement used for decorative or architectural concrete work.

q: 367. Pozzolana is essentially a silicious material containing clay upto
explain: As defined in this text, pozzolana is a siliceous material that may contain clay content up to as much as 80%.

q: 368. For mass concrete in piers and abutments, the concrete mix used is of proportion.
explain: For mass concrete work such as piers and abutments, a leaner mix of proportion 1:3:6 is generally used, as high strength is not the primary requirement.

q: 369. For highly loaded columns, the concrete mix used is of proportion .........:
explain: Highly loaded columns require a rich, high-strength concrete mix, so a proportion of 1:1:2 (equivalent to a high grade) is used.

q: 370. The correct proportioning of various ingredients of concrete largely depend upon.............
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for bulking of sand, water content, and aggregate absorption together — all of these factors affect the actual quantities batched.

q: 371. For high degree of workability, the slump value should vary between
explain: As per the slump classification used in this text, a high degree of workability corresponds to a slump value in the range of 80 to 100 mm.
